I have decrypted the WAL file, applied the WAL transactions to the database, and exported all 11 records to [recovered.json](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-68xt_qkh/recovered.json).

### Summary of Changes
1. **Decrypted WAL File ([main.db-wal](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-68xt_qkh/main.db-wal))**: Inspection of the WAL header (`0x753d44c0` instead of the expected SQLite WAL magic `0x377f0682`, with zero-bytes encoded as `0x42`) showed that the file was XOR-obfuscated with a single-byte key `0x42`. XORing the file bytes with `0x42` restored a valid SQLite Write-Ahead Log.
2. **Database Recovery ([main.db](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-68xt_qkh/main.db))**: Checkpointed the restored WAL file into [main.db](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-68xt_qkh/main.db) (while also preserving the decrypted [main.db-wal](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-68xt_qkh/main.db-wal)), recovering both the updated values for `id` 1 and 2 (`150` and `250`) and the 6 newly inserted rows (`id` 6 through 11).
3. **Exported JSON ([recovered.json](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-68xt_qkh/recovered.json))**: Extracted all 11 records from `items` ordered by `id` and saved them to `/app/recovered.json`.
